title: Reward Models from Scratch
summary: Build and train the reward model that RLHF depends on: turn human comparisons into (prompt, chosen, rejected) triples, then give a transformer a one-number head so it scores a response, and train it so the chosen response scores higher than the rejected one.
objectives: Build preference data as (prompt, chosen, rejected) triples and explain why comparisons are easier to collect than absolute scores
Describe how a reward model reuses a transformer body with a one-number head, and which token's hidden state it reads
Write the pairwise Bradley-Terry loss and compute it by hand for a pair of scores
Train the model and check it by accuracy on held-out pairs
prerequisites: The theory of why we collect comparisons, and the Bradley-Terry model behind them, is in [Preference tuning](/learn/fine-tuning/preference-tuning/why-preferences). You need the SFT prompt template from [SFT from scratch](/learn/post-training/sft-from-scratch).
